subject: Clarify: Order Form Indemnity — Customer Notice & Defense Handoff
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 25 Mar 2025 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: Order Form Indemnity — Customer Notice & Defense Handoff

Team,

Helios (prospect -> likely to sign) just returned a set of order-form redlines. The key point they flagged is the indemnity paragraph: they want primary defense/control for third-party IP claims related to outputs we host for them (they say "model output risk is a product feature"). Procurement is pushing back on language that leaves us with open-ended cooperate-and-reimburse obligations.

Highlights from their redline (attached: redline_v3.docx):
- They propose we accept defense for claims arising from underlying model weights only, and they retain defense for alleged infringement tied to customer prompts or datasets.
- Short notice window (7 days) to trigger defense obligations; they want us to indemnify even if they miss that window.
- They suggest a carveout for "AI-generated outputs" to shift responsibility onto us.

Questions for legal and sales ops:
1) Is there a middle-ground language that limits our exposure but is acceptable commercially (e.g., require prompt notice, give us cooperation rights, allow us to assume defense if we choose)?
2) What evidence will we insist on before accepting defense (logs, payloads, prompt history, trained dataset provenance)?
3) Any procurement constraints for Helios (they want a one-page PO and fast turnaround).

Next steps I suggest: legal drafts 1-2 compromise snippets, sales prepares a short customer-facing rationale, and we propose a single mutual action plan (MAP) with timeline. Can Kimberly take point on suggested wording? Ben/Dev please confirm what evidence we can realistically provide from the platform (audit logs, KV cache snapshots, model name/commit).

Thanks — we should aim to close this before the end of next week.

— Laura
Laura Bennett

Subject: RE: Clarify: Order Form Indemnity — Customer Notice & Defense Handoff

Laura — thanks for the context and the doc. I reviewed Helios's redlines and sketched two compromise options (see inline below and attached redline_suggested.docx):

Option A (preferred, narrower exposure):
- Redwood agrees to indemnify and assume defense only for third-party claims that allege infringement by our model architecture/weights or derivatives we distributed ("Vendor IP Claims").
- For claims tied to customer-provided prompts, data, or customer configurations that materially alter model behavior, Helios will have primary defense (Vendor has cooperation rights and option to assume defense if we reasonably believe the claim implicates Vendor IP).
- Notice: require notice within 30 days of first becoming aware; failure to give timely notice limits remedies except for wilful concealment.
- Evidence: require claim notice, identified allegedly-infringing output (with timestamp), prompt & input payload, model name & version, and relevant audit logs.

Option B (commercial compromise):
- Similar split but allow Helios to request Redwood to assume defense; if Redwood assumes defense, Redwood may seek cost-sharing or reserve the right to tender to insurers. Notice window negotiated down to 14 days if they can guarantee access to output payloads quickly.

A few practical notes:
- We should not accept an "AI-generated outputs" carveout that automatically shifts all output risk to us — too open-ended and impossible to defend operationally.
- The evidence list must map to what Dev can produce within SLA; Ben/Dev — please confirm we'll reliably surface the following: full input payload (+attachments if any), model version, user id, and time-of-generation logs. If not, we must shorten the notice window requirement.
- I moved the failing-notice fallback from absolute liability to a reduction in remedies when notice is late, which is an industry-standard stance and easier to sell.

I'll attach suggested redline snippets. If sales is okay with Option A, legal can seed the customer with that language and we can iterate.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_suggested.docx (legal compromise language)

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha@helios-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 26 Mar 2025 10:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarify: Order Form Indemnity — Customer Notice & Defense Handoff

Hi Laura / Kimberly — thanks for the quick review and suggested options. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) We are trying to protect our enterprise customers. If a downstream customer asserts infringement based on model output (e.g., a generated policy that reproduces a third-party clause), we need a path to remediation that doesn't put our entire business at risk.

2) We are comfortable with Helios retaining primary defense for claims that are demonstrably caused by our prompts/configuration, but we are wary of a 30-day truncated notice — in practice, our customers sometimes discover issues later. Can we accept 60 days for notice but keep the ability to request Vendor to assume defense if it appears the model/weights are responsible?

3) Evidence: we can provide the alleged output and a customer complaint, but we don't currently log full prompts persistently for privacy reasons. We can keep short-term prompt history (30 days) and are open to negotiating retention for cases that escalate.

4) Liability cap: our procurement team asks that indemnity for IP claims be subject to a cap tied to the order form value (they proposed 2x the annual subscription value).

Happy to take a quick sync tomorrow to walk through if that helps. We're trying to keep the contract compact — the one-page PO is still their preference.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Legal Operations, Helios Analytics

Samantha — really appreciate the detail. Quick summary and proposed MAP: 

Summary of agreed principles:
- Split defense: Helios retains primary defense for claims tied to customer prompts/configs; Redwood will indemnify for Vendor IP Claims (weights/architecture) and may assume defense where evidence points to Vendor IP.
- Notice window: propose 45 days as a compromise (Redwood needs time to triage; Helios needs flexibility). If Helios can commit to longer prompt retention for escalations, we can revisit to 60 days.
- Evidence required: claim notice, the allegedly-infringing output (timestamped), model name/version, any available prompt/input payload, and relevant platform audit logs. If prompt retention is limited, we will rely on available logs and the parties will cooperate to reconstruct the incident.
- Liability cap: Redwood requests that IP indemnity remain uncapped only in cases of wilful misconduct; otherwise cap at 2x annual subscription value is a reasonable commercial point — but any change beyond 2x will require exec approval.

Action items / MAP: 
1) Legal (Kimberly) to deliver a redline with the split-defense language and 45-day notice (deliverable: redline_suggested.docx). Due: EOD Thu 27 Mar.
2) Dev (Dev Patel) to confirm what payloads/logs we can produce within 48 hours and whether we can extend prompt retention for escalations (deliverable: evidence_matrix.xlsx). Due: EOD Thu 27 Mar.
3) Sales/Procurement (Ben) to confirm the customer's PO cadence and whether Helios is willing to accept an addendum for extended prompt retention in exchange for longer notice. Due: Fri 28 Mar.
4) If redline is acceptable, Laura to coordinate a 30-minute sync (video link below) between Helios procurement/legal and Redwood legal/procurement to finalize.

Proposed meeting: Thu 27 Mar 2025 10:00am PT — https://meet.redwood.com/rooms/helios-indemnity-sync

If that timeline works I'll queue the redline and loop in finance for any exec approval on caps if required.

Thanks — Laura
